page: Amazon Web Services c9g.16xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by custom 64-core ARMv9 AWS Graviton Neoverse-V3 processors running at 3.3 GHz. Built on the AWS Nitro System architecture, the system provides 64 dedicated physical CPU cores without hyperthreading, alongside a cache topology featuring 64 KB L1d, 2 MB L2, and 48 MB L3 cache. The instance is provisioned with 128.0 GB of RAM, yielding a compute-dense allocation ratio of 2.0 GB of memory per core. Local NVMe storage is omitted in favor of network storage, while baseline network throughput reaches 34 Gbps.

Benchmark data demonstrates top-tier multi-threaded CPU efficiency and resource density. The server achieves top-tier performance in multi-core stress tests, software compilation with Clang, ray tracing, and data compression workloads such as Gzip and Bzip3 decompression. High memory bandwidth supports notable throughput in Redis SET operations and static web serving workloads. However, instruction sets lacking x86-specific vector extensions and single-threaded constraints place LLM prompt processing and text generation inference speeds in the middle benchmark tier.

The hardware configuration delivers dedicated core execution without hyperthreading overhead, optimizing resource efficiency for highly parallel compute profiles. Omitting local NVMe disks minimizes hardware overhead for compute-focused tasks relying on centralized network storage. Amazon Web Services c9g.16xlarge is well suited for software compilation pipelines, web serving fleets, in-memory key-value databases like Redis, and parallel batch processing.
description: Amazon Web Services c9g.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance equipped with 64 dedicated ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 physical cores operating at 3.3 GHz and 128.0 GB of RAM. Built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor without hyperthreading, it features a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio, a 48 MB L3 cache, baseline network bandwidth of 34 Gbps, and no local NVMe storage. Benchmarks place the system in the top tier for multi-core processing, software compilation, data decompression, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput. Read and write memory bandwidth performance rank in the top quartile, whereas single-core stress performance and small-to-medium model LLM inference speeds sit in the middle tier. By providing dense dedicated core allocation without hyperthreading contention or local disk overhead, the server offers efficient core scaling. Amazon Web Services c9g.16xlarge is effective for batch processing, CI/CD build clusters, web server fleets, and high-throughput key-value databases.
